findings.evidence: Lines 71, 80, and 91 declare `private theorem measurable_max`, `measurable_min`, and `aemeasurable_max`; line 102 alone declares public `theorem aemeasurable_min`. All four statements mention only Mathlib types and their proofs are independent of the distribution theory.
findings.fix: Relocate and publicly expose a coherent finite `inf'`/`sup'` measurability API in an earlier general measure-theory module, then use it here and in `Exponential`.
findings.issue: `aemeasurable_min` is exported while the parallel `aemeasurable_max` and general `measurable_min`/`measurable_max` results remain private, despite this file developing both extrema; consumers cannot use the corresponding generic facts.

summary: The newly public measurability API is asymmetric and leaves equally general finite-extrema infrastructure private.
